simple.meaning: נְשָׁמָה (nᵉshâmâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a puff , i.e. wind , angry or vital breath , divine inspiration , intellect . or (concretely) an animal.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 2:7. The surrounding context includes death, kingship, land, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נְשָׁמָה (H5397) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

definitions.short: a puff , i.e. wind , angry or vital breath , divine inspiration , intellect . or (concretely) an animal
definitions.full: H5397. neshamah נְשָׁמָה noun feminine breath ; — ׳נ Deut 20:16 9 t.; construct נִשְׁמַת (compare Lag BN 82 ) Gen 2:7 10 t.; suffix נִשְׁמָתִי Job 27:3 ; נִשְׁמָתוֺ 34:14 ; plural נְשָׁמוֺת Isa 57:16 ; — 1 breath of God as hot wind kindling a flame Isa 30:33 ; as destroying wind 2Sam 22:16 = Psa 18:16 ; Job 4:9 ; as cold wind producing ice 32:8 ; 33:4 . 2 breath of man 1Kin 17:17 ; Isa 42:5 ; Job 27:3 ; Dan 10:7 ; breath of life חיים נשׁמת Gen 2:7 (J); compare חַיִּים רוּחַ נִשְׁמַת 7:22 (J); as breathed in by God it is God's breath in man Job 34:14 ; 36:4 ; and is characteristic of man באפו נשׁמה אשׁר אדם Isa 2:22 man in whose nostrils is but a breath (late gloss). 3 synonym נְשָׁמָה כָּל נפשׁ every breathing thing Deut 20:16 ; Josh 11:11 , 14 ; 1Kin 15:29 ; כָּלהַֿנְּשָׁמָה Josh 10:14 ; Psa 150:6 ; נְשָׁמוֺת Isa 57:16 . 4 spirit of man, || י ׳נֵר ׳נ אָדָם רוּחַ, Prov 20:27 the spirit of man is a lamp of ׳י .

occurrences.englishText: Yahweh God formed man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
All on the dry land, in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of life, died.
But of the cities of these peoples that Yahweh your God gives you for an inheritance, you shall save alive nothing that breathes;

So Joshua struck all the land, the hill country, the South, the lowland, the slopes, and all their kings. He left no one remaining, but he utterly destroyed all that breathed, as Yahweh, the God of Israel, commanded.
They struck all the souls who were in it with the edge of the sword, utterly destroying them. There was no one left who breathed. He burned Hazor with fire.

The children of Israel took all the plunder of these cities, with the livestock, as plunder for themselves; but every man they struck with the edge of the sword, until they had destroyed them. They didn’t leave any who breathed.
Then the channels of the sea appeared.

As soon as he was king, he struck all the house of Jeroboam. He didn’t leave to Jeroboam any who breathed, until he had destroyed him; according to the saying of Yahweh, which he spoke by his servant Ahijah the Shilonite;
After these things, the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, became sick; and his sickness was so severe that there was no breath left in him.
By the breath of God they perish.
To whom have you uttered words?
(for the length of my life is still in me,
But there is a spirit in man,
The Spirit of God has made me,
If he set his heart on himself,
By the breath of God, ice is given,
He sent from on high.
Let everything that has breath praise Yah!
The spirit of man is Yahweh’s lamp,
Stop trusting in man, whose breath is in his nostrils;
For his burning place has long been ready. Yes, for the king it is prepared. He has made its pyre deep and large with fire and much wood. Yahweh’s breath, like a stream of sulfur, kindles it.
God Yahweh,
For I will not contend forever, neither will I always be angry;
For how can the servant of this my lord talk with this my lord? For as for me, immediately there remained no strength in me. There was no breath left in me.”
